queries: housing market days on market trend

findings.claim: In August 2026 the median US home spent 60 days on market, unchanged from a year earlier, while active inventory rose 3.6% year over year to 1,140,035 listings.
findings.sourceTitle: Delistings Trend Below Last Year's Pace As Summer Comes to an End: Realtor.com August Housing Report

findings.claim: The national median list price was $424,500 in August 2026, down 1.3% year over year, the tenth consecutive month of annual list-price declines.

20.4% of active listings carried a price reduction in August 2026, roughly one in five homes on the market cutting its asking price. Cuts were least common in the Northeast at 14.1% and most common in the West at 22.0%.
Summer 2026 delistings ran 12.6% below last year's pace, meaning sellers are staying on the market and competing rather than pulling their listings as they did in summer 2025.

Realtor.com named September 27 to October 3, 2026 the best week of the year to buy: active listings 13.3% above the average week and 31.9% above the start of the year, buyer competition 30.1% below its annual peak, and listing prices 3.5% below the seasonal peak, about $14,000 off a median $416,000 home.
findings.sourceTitle: Realtor.com: September 27th to October 3rd Marks the Best Time to Buy a Home in 2026

findings.claim: During the week of September 27 to October 3, 2026, homes are expected to sit about 64 days on market, roughly 13 days longer than the year's fastest pace.
findings.sourceTitle: Realtor.com: Best Time to Buy a Home in 2026

findings.claim: The 30-year fixed mortgage averaged 6.76% for the week of September 10, 2026, up from 6.71% the prior week and above 6.35% a year earlier.
findings.sourceTitle: Mortgage Rates Average 6.76%, Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey

findings.claim: In NAR's 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers, 81% of buyers rated listing photos the most useful feature of their online home search.
findings.sourceTitle: How to Maximize Online Visibility for Every Listing, National Association of REALTORS

findings.claim: NAR's February 2025 Profile of Home Staging found 83% of buyers' agents said staging made it easier for a buyer to visualize a property as their future home, and 26% said staging affected most buyers' view of the home.
findings.sourceTitle: Profile of Home Staging, National Association of REALTORS

findings.claim: In NAR's February 2025 staging survey the most commonly staged rooms were the living room at 91%, the primary bedroom at 83% and the dining room at 69%.
findings.sourceTitle: Profile of Home Staging, National Association of REALTORS

findings.claim: Only 21% of sellers' agents staged every home before listing it, per NAR's February 2025 staging survey, so most listings still go online unstaged.
findings.sourceTitle: Profile of Home Staging, National Association of REALTORS

findings.claim: A 2026 vendor cost comparison puts traditional staging at $2,000 to $5,000 plus to set up plus $500 to $2,000 a month in furniture rental over 3 to 7 business days, against $75 to $600 for a whole virtually staged listing delivered in 24 to 48 hours.
findings.sourceTitle: Virtual staging vs traditional staging: a 2026 cost-benefit analysis, Virtuance
findings.confidence: vendor-blog, commercial slant, attribute as industry analysis

findings.claim: On a $400,000 listing, a 2026 industry analysis modelled traditional staging at roughly $4,500 against a 1% price lift of $4,000, a net loss of about $500, while the same lift on $300 of virtual staging nets about $3,700.
findings.sourceTitle: Virtual staging vs traditional staging: a 2026 cost-benefit analysis, Virtuance
findings.confidence: vendor-blog, commercial slant, attribute as industry analysis

findings.claim: A 2026 real estate photography roundup reports buyers spend about 2.7 seconds on a listing's primary photo before clicking in or scrolling past, and under 20 seconds deciding whether the listing deserves a deeper look.
findings.sourceTitle: Real Estate Photography Statistics Every Agent Should Know in 2026, Modern Angles

findings.claim: Researcher note: widely repeated staging stats such as staged homes selling 73% faster, selling for 25% more, or a virtual staging ROI of 3,650% were deliberately excluded because no page repeating them cites a primary study.
findings.sourceTitle: Exclusion note, checked against NAR Profile of Home Staging
